Class SqlSession

java.lang.Object
org.cobol4j.SqlSession
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class SqlSession extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A scoped SQL session — acquires a connection on creation, releases it on close.

Two usage patterns are supported:

1. Explicit try-with-resources (you control the flow): 

try (SqlSession session = SqlSession.from(factory)) {
    session.sql().select(...).param(...).into(...).execute();
    session.sql().execute(...).param(...).execute();
    session.commit();
}
// Connection automatically released (returned to pool or closed)

2. Unit-of-work lambda (the session manages the lifecycle): 

SqlSession.work(factory, session -> {
    session.sql().select(...).param(...).into(...).execute();
    session.sql().execute(...).param(...).execute();
    // commit happens automatically at end of block
});
// on success: commit + release
// on exception: rollback + release, then rethrow or handle

In both patterns, if the session closes without a commit, the connection is rolled back before release.

    • from

      public static SqlSession from(ConnectionFactory factory)
      Create a session by acquiring a connection from the factory.

    • work

      public static void work(ConnectionFactory factory, Consumer<SqlSession> work)
      Execute a unit of work with managed lifecycle: acquire → work → commit → release (on success) acquire → work → rollback → release → rethrow (on failure)

      This is the equivalent of: 

      try {
    conn = factory.acquire();
    // ... work ...
    conn.commit();
} catch (Exception ex) {
    conn.rollback();
    throw ex;
} finally {
    conn.release();
}

    • work

      public static void work(ConnectionFactory factory, Consumer<SqlSession> work, Consumer<Exception> errorHandler)
      Execute a unit of work with a custom error handler instead of rethrowing. The error handler receives the exception after rollback, allowing logging or status-flag updates without propagating the exception.
